6.             The only question which requires 

determination in this petition is that whether Talaq 

becomes effective after expiration of ninety days 

from the date of pronouncement of Talaq or from 

the date notice to the Chairman Arbitration Council. 

No doubt according to sub section 3 of section 7 of 

the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 divorce 

shall not be effected until the expiration of ninety 

days from the date on which notice was delivered to 

the Chairman but the Shariat Appellate Bench of the 

Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan in case reported 

as <u>**Allah Dad ..Vs.. Mukhtar and another (1992**</u> 

<u>**SCMR 1273)**</u> has declared that *“ineffectiveness of*

was further laid down in the said judgment that:- 

*“ It is now evident that a notice of Talaq* 

*to the Chairman is not mandatory under the Injunctions of Islam and any divorce pronounced or written by a husband cannot be ineffective or invalid in Shariah merely because its notice has not been given to the Chairman, therefore, if a woman after obtaining a divorce from her husband and after the necessary period of ‘Iddat’ ; contracts a marriage with a third person, their marriage cannot be held as invalid marriage, at least for the purpose of the Ordinance.”* 

7. 

In the light of the aforesaid esteemed 

judgment of the Shariat Appellate Bench of the 

Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan, the issuance of 

notice of divorce to the Chairman as envisaged in 

Section-7 ibid is not mandatory, therefore, the 

simple answer of the aforesaid formulated question 

would be that divorce would become effective after 

expiry of ninety days from the date of 

pronouncement of divorce and not from the date of 

issuance of notice to the Chairman Arbitration 

Council.

#                       <u>**ORDER SHEET**</u> 

## <u>**IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT LAHORE**</u> 

##                <u>**JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT**</u> 

<u>**Case No:   Writ Petition No.23303/13**</u> 

<u>**Naheed Sidique**</u> 

<u>**Versus DDO Litigation etc.**</u>  

02.12.2013 Ch. Fayyaz Ahmad Advocate for the petitioner.  

 Mr. Inam ul Islam Advocate for respondent No.4. 

    Facts necessitating for filing of instant 

Constitutional petition are that the petitioner was 

married with respondent No.4 on 24.03.1995 and 

out of the wedlock no issue was born. The 

relationship between the parties became strained and 

on 18.03.2013 respondent No.4 pronounced Talaq-

e-Salasa to the petitioner in the presence of 

witnesses and also sent a notice to the Chairman 

Arbitration Council, U.C. No.120, Ali Raza Abad, 

Lahore. On 20.06.2013 respondent No.4 gave a 

notice of withdrawal of Talaq, which was duly 

contested by the petitioner stating that after expiry 

of ninety days it became irrevocable. In order to 

resolve the controversy the Administrator/Chairman 

referred the matter to respondent No.1 for legal 

---

Writ Petition No.23303/13 

2

opinion, who vide endorsement dated 10.07.2013 

gave the following legal opinion:- 

*“The revocation of Divorce is within the* 

*prescribed period of 90 days. The divorce would not be effected. The Union Council can stop the proceedings.”* 

2. 

Being unhappy with the said legal 

opinion the petitioner has filed instant Constitutional 

petition.  

3. 

Learned counsel for the petitioner 

submits that respondent No.4 pronounced Talaq on 

18.03.2013 and it became effective after expiry of 

90 days i.e. 17.06.2013; that legal opinion of 

respondent No.1 that revocation is within time is 

illegal; that period of Iddat of ninety days is to be 

counted from the date of pronouncement of Talaq 

and not from the date of issuance of notice of Talaq 

to the Chairman Arbitration Council; that 

respondent No.4 in order to harass the petitioner 

issued revocation notice after expiry of requisite 

period.  

4. 

Conversely, learned counsel for 

respondent No.4 submits that although the divorce 

was pronounced on 18.03.2013 but its notice was 

served upon the Chairman Arbitration Council on 

---

Writ Petition No.23303/13 

3

20.03.2013; that according to sub section 3 of 

Section 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 

1961 period of Iddat of ninety days is to be counted 

from the date of notice to the Chairman Arbitration 

Council and not from the date of pronouncement of 

divorce; that opinion of respondent No.1 is in 

consonance with the relevant provisions of law and 

no occasion arises for this Court to intervene with 

the same in its Constitutional jurisdiction.  

5.                    Arguments heard. Record perused. 

6.             The only question which requires 

determination in this petition is that whether Talaq 

becomes effective after expiration of ninety days 

from the date of pronouncement of Talaq or from 

the date notice to the Chairman Arbitration Council. 

No doubt according to sub section 3 of section 7 of 

the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 divorce 

shall not be effected until the expiration of ninety 

days from the date on which notice was delivered to 

the Chairman but the Shariat Appellate Bench of the 

Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan in case reported 

as <u>**Allah Dad ..Vs.. Mukhtar and another (1992**</u> 

<u>**SCMR 1273)**</u> has declared that *“ineffectiveness of* 

*Talaq in the absence of a notice to the Chairman, as* 

---

Writ Petition No.23303/13 

4

*envisaged by section 7 of the Family Laws* 

*Ordinance, is against the Injunctions of Islam.”* It 

was further laid down in the said judgment that:- 

*“ It is now evident that a notice of Talaq* 

*to the Chairman is not mandatory under the Injunctions of Islam and any divorce pronounced or written by a husband cannot be ineffective or invalid in Shariah merely because its notice has not been given to the Chairman, therefore, if a woman after obtaining a divorce from her husband and after the necessary period of ‘Iddat’ ; contracts a marriage with a third person, their marriage cannot be held as invalid marriage, at least for the purpose of the Ordinance.”* 

7. 

In the light of the aforesaid esteemed 

judgment of the Shariat Appellate Bench of the 

Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan, the issuance of 

notice of divorce to the Chairman as envisaged in 

Section-7 ibid is not mandatory, therefore, the 

simple answer of the aforesaid formulated question 

would be that divorce would become effective after 

expiry of ninety days from the date of 

pronouncement of divorce and not from the date of 

issuance of notice to the Chairman Arbitration 

Council.  

---

Writ Petition No.23303/13 

5

8. 

In the present case, admittedly, 

respondent No.4 pronounced Talaq to the petitioner 

on 18.03.2013, therefore, period of Iddat of ninety 

days expired on 17.06.2013 and Talaq was 

irrevocable on 20.06.2013 the date when notice for 

withdrawal of divorce was issued by respondent 

No.4.  

9. 

For the reasons discussed above, this 

writ petition is <u>**allowed**</u> and consequently legal 

opinion of respondent No.1 dated 10.07.2013 is 

declared illegal and contrary to law. Respondent 

No.2/Chairman Arbitration Council, U.C. No.120, 

Ali Raza Abad, Lahore is directed to issue requisite 

divorce certificate to the petitioner forthwith. Parties 

shall bear their own costs.  

                     <u>**(Muhammad Farrukh Irfan Khan)**</u> 

*Azam 

                         <u>**Judge**</u>
